title: Showdown Challenges
meta: Every option meets the same learning outcomes
intro: Students enjoy the food challenges most, and we are keen to learn how cooking together shapes their experience. If your school allows it, we encourage Decorate, Bake or Mystery.

details: Teams of 2–3 at tables; no kitchen or oven
Print the cards and worksheets; gather paper and colouring supplies
One paper cupcake design per team
Premade cupcakes and frosting; a craft backup with no food
Teams of 2–3; no oven; hand-washing, plates and wipes
Buy cupcakes the day before, one per student or one per team
Decorated cupcakes to eat, take home or display
45–60 min; whole lesson about 60–75 min, plus cooling
The chocolate cupcake recipe: no eggs or dairy, contains wheat flour
Teams of 3–5 by oven space; an oven and an adult to run it
Book the oven; buy one recipe per team (12–18 cupcakes each)
A batch of cupcakes per team, still warm at the end
The most: bowls, pans and stations
A mix-in ingredient, a missing measuring cup, or a half batch
Same time, food and prep as Bake

blocks.title: Before any food challenge
blocks.text: Check your school’s food rules and every student’s allergies and dietary needs against each label, including any mystery ingredient.
